summary: The testing and review intent is clear, but the ADR is not yet implementable as tooling: its biggest gap is where measurement and field-run records live, what shape they take, and who produces them.

questions.text: What shape do recorded measurements take, and where are they stored (committed structured data, CI artifacts, or notes)?
questions.reason: Baseline comparison across scales and cold/warm caches needs a stable persisted record; the ADR lists what to measure but gives no format or location.

questions.text: Where are field-run records kept, failed attempts included, what does one record contain, and does ADR 0024 or this ADR own that format?
questions.reason: Preserving unsuccessful runs needs a durable store and run/attempt identity; the ADR says to pair MCP telemetry with an experience report via ADR 0024 scenarios and to keep failed runs, but not where or how.

questions.text: Is MCP/agent telemetry part of the shipped runtime or only instrumentation in a test/field harness?
questions.reason: A shipped feature needs a data model, default, storage and privacy boundary behind a host effect; the ADR only says to 'pair MCP telemetry with an experience report'.

questions.text: Must routine test entry points actively refuse provider access (an enforcing handler), or is not wiring providers by convention enough?
questions.reason: An enforcing guard is a runtime component with its own failure semantics; the ADR says only 'No direct provider access in routine tests'.

questions.text: Is the pre-implementation boundary review packet a persisted, checked artifact, and if so where does it live and must its authored example be an executable test?
questions.reason: Decides whether to build a per-boundary layout and presence check or nothing; the ADR lists the packet's contents and says 'no mandatory contributor governance beyond normal tests and review', leaning review-only without saying so.

questions.text: How are opt-in provider integration runs selected (env flag, separate target, CI job), and do they use the product's local secret store or a separate test credential source?
questions.reason: Changes test tagging and configuration; the ADR requires 'explicit opt-in integration runs' but names no mechanism or credential source.

questions.text: May production code carry test-only fault-injection seams for the process/Git fault tests, or must faults be injected purely from outside?
questions.reason: Seams change public effect signatures and handler composition of storage/acceptance boundaries; the ADR requires 'real process/Git fault tests' but also removal of 'unused interfaces'.

questions.text: Must every effect boundary have a deterministic in-memory interpreter alongside its native handler, or only where a test needs one?
questions.reason: Determines whether each boundary carries two handlers plus conformance tests; the ADR lists 'deterministic semantic interpreters' among checks while requiring a current obligation for each mechanism and removal of alternate implementations.
